missing_or_wrong: Turn 1 invents a visible text on Michelle's phone ('Meet me at the lab at 4:00am. -Shelly') that conflicts with the opening/canon, which only says Michelle sent an early-morning text and that calls/texts were missed amid emergency alerts.
Turn 1 says the phone screen is cracked, but canon says the phone is undamaged.
Turn 1 asserts details not established in-scene as observed discoveries ('chair is tipped over', 'nothing else was taken', 'someone came for Michelle') instead of local evidence.
Turn 2 searches the workstation drawer but fails to state what item was found; it withholds actionable discovery from the player.
Turn 2 also leaps to interpretation about initials/instruction without naming the object or contents, so the assigned investigative beat is poorly dramatized.
Turn 3 ignores the requested object/context from Turn 2 and reverts to the kitchen phone, creating continuity confusion about where the damaged recording came from.
Turn 3 reveals protected knowledge too baldly ('It warns Kristin not to trust emergency broadcasts') without the intervening concrete recovery/listening scene the player earned.

Turn 4 has officers spontaneously appear and asks the player to 'Listen to the officers ask about her research,' but the narration mostly gives generic dialogue and then summary; it does not dramatize how they know about the research.
Turn 5 exits the scene by reading 'the rest of the files,' but those files were never clearly found/read in prior turns because Turn 2 failed to reveal the discovered medium and Turn 3 mishandled it.
Turn 5 leaves the scene without properly motivating the exit in narrated prose grounded in an actually established discovery from this scene.
Across the scene, Michelle's unsearched work area is not properly investigated in a responsive, rewarding way despite repeated apt searching requests.
The scene races to future beats and transitions via summaries ('someone came for Michelle', bench exchange point, travel there) instead of progressive local revelation.
reasons: The scene violates scene-local canon consistency on key physical facts: Michelle's phone is undamaged in canon, yet Turn 1 makes it cracked.
The opening and situation establish only that an early-morning text was missed; inventing its exact content and sender label ('-Shelly') is unsupported and changes the mystery.
Interactive responsiveness is weak: searching the kitchen largely repeats setup, and searching the workstation drawer does not tell the player what was discovered, so investigation is not rewarded.
Progressive revelation fails because the scene both withholds earned local findings (Turn 2) and blurts higher-level conclusions or future leads in summary form (Turns 3 and 5).
Protected knowledge is not kept safe: the emergency-broadcast warning is delivered as a flat fact before the scene has convincingly recovered and played the interrupted message in-text.

The authored beats are not cleanly covered in order. The workstation/research discovery beat is muddled, then the recording/file beats are inconsistently handled, then the exit jumps to the park bench lead without a solid narrated chain of discovery.

The departure turn does not satisfy the exit requirement: although it names a bench exchange point, that point is not established through player-readable discovery in prior narration, so the reason to leave is not properly earned.
